classification.difficultyReason: Use the given factors to locate intercepts and sketch an upward parabola, then translate its zero, below-axis and above-axis regions into solutions, excluding roots from the strict inequalities.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Sketch the graph of $y=(x-2)(x+1)$, labelling the $x$-intercepts. You do not need to find the coordinates of the vertex.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}(x-2)(x+1)&=0\\x&=2\text{ or }x=-1\end{align*}$$
The coefficient of $x^2$ is positive, so the parabola opens upwards. At $x=0$, $y=(-2)(1)=-2$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 8(a); answer book PDF page 24 Q8(a)
spec.description: Equation-driven parabola with source-key x-intercepts -1 and 2 and y-intercept -2. Vertex coordinates are intentionally unlabelled.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Hence, state the value(s) of $x$ for which

answer.worked: The graph meets the $x$-axis at $x=-1$ and $x=2$. Hence $(x-2)(x+1)=0$ at these values.
The graph lies below the $x$-axis between its intercepts. Hence $-1<x<2$.
The graph lies above the $x$-axis outside its intercepts. Hence $x<-1$ or $x>2$.
